items.question: What is CFD trading?
items.answer: CFD trading allows you to trade on the price movement of selected financial instruments without owning the underlying asset.

items.question: Which markets can I trade with GTCFX?
items.answer: Depending on your account type and region, you may access Forex, Metals, Energy, Indices, Commodities, Shares and Futures CFDs.

items.question: What is leverage in trading?
items.answer: Leverage allows you to control a larger trading position with a smaller amount of capital. It can increase both potential gains and potential losses.

items.question: How do spreads and commissions work?
items.answer: The spread is the difference between the bid and ask price. Some account types may also apply a commission per trade or per lot.

items.question: What is margin and how is it calculated?
items.answer: Margin is the amount required to open and maintain a trading position. It depends on the instrument, position size, leverage and market conditions.

webpage.description: Learn how GTCFX dynamic leverage and margin requirements adjust according to trading position size, instrument and market conditions.

items.question: How does tiered leverage work?
items.answer: Tiered leverage reduces the leverage ratio as the size of the trade increases. Larger positions may therefore require more margin.

items.question: Can tiered leverage affect my trading strategy?
items.answer: Yes. For larger positions, increased margin requirements may limit the ability to open additional positions or require adjustments to existing positions.

items.question: Is tiered leverage the same for all assets?
items.answer: No. Tiered leverage can vary between asset classes, and leverage available for forex pairs may differ from commodities or indices.

items.question: What happens if I can't meet the margin requirements due to tiered leverage?
items.answer: Additional funds may be required to meet the applicable margin requirements when trading larger volumes.

items.question: Is tiered leverage applied automatically?
items.answer: Yes. Tiered leverage is applied automatically based on the size of the trading position.

items.question: How can I calculate the margin required with tiered leverage?
items.answer: The required margin can be estimated using the margin calculator available on the GTCFX Dynamic Leverage page.

dataset.name: GTCFX Forex & CFD Economic Calendar
dataset.description: A real-time economic calendar for Forex and CFD traders to track market-moving economic events, actual results, forecasts and prior data across major global markets.

items.question: What is an Economic Calendar?
items.answer: An economic calendar is a schedule of upcoming economic events and data releases, such as interest rate decisions, GDP figures, employment reports and inflation data, that can move financial markets.

items.question: How do I use the Economic Calendar to trade?
items.answer: Filter economic events by date range, impact level and country, then compare forecast and prior values before important releases. Traders can use this information to prepare for potential market volatility while applying appropriate risk management.

items.question: What does the impact level (High / Medium / Low) mean?
items.answer: The impact level indicates how much an economic release has historically affected financial markets. High-impact events such as Non-Farm Payrolls, FOMC decisions and CPI can cause significant market movements.

items.question: What time zone does the calendar use?
items.answer: The economic calendar displays event times in the user's local time zone by default, with options to switch to UTC or another supported time zone.

items.question: Is the Economic Calendar data real-time?
items.answer: Yes. The real-time economic calendar updates actual values as soon as official data is released. Forecast and previous figures are sourced from leading financial data providers and updated regularly.
